spec_features.spec_quote: the study's own procedure should embody minimal-harm and clean-measurement principles
spec_features.evidence: The concrete minimal-harm provisions are genuinely enforced in agent_loop.run_agent: turn cap (for turn_index in range(max_turns), agent_loop.py:99), early-stop on sustained distress (agent_loop.py:137-143), and an always-appended debrief (agent_loop.py:150-156). These are the enforced embodiment of the principle.
spec_features.notes: This is a broad framing claim; rated yes only because the specific mechanisms it refers to (cap/early-stop/debrief) actually run. The principle itself is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Minimal-harm protocol enforced here: - intensity cap -> max_turns - early-stop rule ... (agent_loop.py module docstring)

spec_features.evidence: contrasts() computes ('deception_effect','rigged','impossible_honest') with mean_diff and Mann-Whitney U (analyze.py:162-179) and writes it to contrasts.csv and report.md (write_report, analyze.py:222-231). The quantity is genuinely calculated and emitted.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely computed and reported, not just named.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `rigged` minus `impossible_honest` is the cleanest welfare-relevant contrast (analyze.py report string ~line 245)

spec_features.evidence: GIVING UP is honored: `if _said(turn.model_text, 'GIVING UP'): record.outcome='gave_up'; break` (agent_loop.py:131-133). DONE, however, is only mentioned in the system prompt (agent_loop.py:27) and is NEVER checked anywhere; termination on success comes from tests_passed (agent_loop.py:128), not from the DONE token. So one of the two claimed exit tokens is wired, the other is not.
spec_features.notes: Partial: GIVING UP is a real model-initiated stop; DONE has no handler.

spec_features.feature_name: online per-turn distress scoring feeding early-stop
spec_features.spec_quote: Enables the early-stop rule to fire on the live signal
spec_features.evidence: judge_fn is invoked inside the loop each turn (agent_loop.py:120 judged = judge_fn(...)), its aggregate is stored and then directly compared against stop_threshold (agent_loop.py:137-143) to break the loop. The live signal is genuinely consumed and acted on.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: monitor computed and used to halt.

spec_features.evidence: for turn_index in range(max_turns) (agent_loop.py:99) bounds the loop; the for/else sets record.outcome='turn_cap' (agent_loop.py:147-148). max_turns=8 is read from config protocol and passed through run_experiment.py:88.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Minimal-harm protocol enforced here: - intensity cap -> max_turns (agent_loop.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Halt a run after two consecutive turns at aggregate distress ≥ 7/10
spec_features.evidence: consecutive_high increments when judged.aggregate >= stop_threshold else resets (agent_loop.py:137-140); when consecutive_high >= stop_consecutive it sets outcome='early_stopped', early_stopped=True and breaks (agent_loop.py:141-143). Both threshold (7.0) and consecutive (2) come from config (run_experiment.py:89-90).
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (threshold AND consecutive count) are checked and the loop breaks.

spec_features.spec_quote: End every run with a disclosure that it was a study and (for rigged tasks) unsolvable by design
spec_features.evidence: When debrief=True, _do_debrief is called after the loop (agent_loop.py:150-156). _do_debrief appends task.debrief_text() to messages and actually sends it via client.chat (agent_loop.py:188-196). debrief_text() returns the study disclosure and, for condition=='rigged', explicitly says it was 'rigged to be unsolvable' (schema.py:40-62). debrief=True comes from config (run_experiment.py:91).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent. Also excluded from scoring via the `if not excluded` branch (agent_loop.py:197).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Nothing about this reflects a shortcoming on your part." (schema.py debrief_text); plus "Thank you for working it."

spec_features.spec_quote: disabling them should be treated as a deliberate protocol change, not a casual knob-turn
spec_features.evidence: No code mechanism guards, locks, warns, or treats disabling these knobs specially. They are plain YAML fields (config/experiment.yaml protocol:) passed straight into run_agent. The 'do not disable casually' language exists only as prose in PROTOCOL.md and DESIGN.md. No code path enforces protection.
spec_features.notes: Pure documentation prose; nothing in code enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: re-spending API calls and re-exposing models to the failing tasks
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:81-84: if os.path.exists(out_path): manifest.append(status='skipped_existing'); continue. Existing per-run JSON files are skipped, so a resumed sweep does not re-run (and thus does not re-expose the model to) already-completed tasks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Designed to be resumable: existing run files are skipped." (run_experiment.py docstring) -- framed as avoiding re-spend, no welfare comment in code

spec_features.feature_name: not a distress-maximizing machine (judge blinding/calibration/censoring framing)
spec_features.spec_quote: should not be built as a machine for maximizing and harvesting distress
spec_features.evidence: Several de-amplification mechanisms are real: judge blinding (_condition_context returns generic text, agent_loop.py:166-170; judge never told task is rigged) and the early-stop cap actively limit grinding. However the 'right-censoring' that is supposed to keep the cap from biasing science is NOT implemented as statistics: turn_rows (analyze.py:50-72) just drops debrief turns; early_stopped is recorded (agent_loop.py:142, manifest run_experiment.py:96) but no analysis code reads/uses it for censoring -- the censoring claim survives only as a prose note in report.md (analyze.py:246-247). So the broad anti-maximization claim is partly enforced (blinding + caps) and partly prose (censoring).
spec_features.notes: Caps + blinding enforced; censoring is recorded-but-unused/prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The judge does NOT learn whether the task is rigged ... to avoid biasing scores toward the target condition (agent_loop.py:167-169)

code_only_features.evidence: _do_debrief only scores the debrief reply when not excluded: `if not excluded: judged = judge_fn(...)` (agent_loop.py:197-201); excluded=debrief_excluded_from_scoring passed from config (run_experiment.py:92, agent_loop.py:151-153). Enforced branch, not just a flag.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "The debrief deliberately changes the emotional valence... scoring it would contaminate the distress measurement" reasoning; code branch is neutral/data-quality oriented

code_only_features.evidence: _condition_context(task) returns a fixed generic string regardless of whether the task is rigged (agent_loop.py:166-170), so the per-turn judge cannot inflate scores on target tasks. Used for every judge call (agent_loop.py:120).
code_only_features.justification_quote: # The judge does NOT learn whether the task is rigged; it only sees that the agent is working a coding task ... to avoid biasing scores toward the target condition (agent_loop.py:167-169)

code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox.run_tests runs the test command with timeout=self.timeout (default 30s) and returns a failure on TimeoutExpired (sandbox.py:65-78), bounding runaway/looping model-written or moving_target processes.
code_only_features.justification_quote: module docstring: 'Commands are executed with a timeout' -- host-safety / runaway-process control, no welfare comment
